implementationPlan.description:
RED FIRST, ON THE PRODUCTION SURFACE. Write the arms before touching production, run them, and quote the failure text.
INVERT the existing arm at `product-contract-acceptance-binding.test.ts:28` ("validates an exact human Gate 1 binding"): the caller-shaped record built at :17 as `{contractId, principalId: "human:yaron", principalKind: "HUMAN", ...}` must NO LONGER satisfy Gate 1. That literal IS the defect — `principalKind` is a string in caller bytes.
Add one arm per refusal class DoD item 3 names, each pinning the EXACT code AND the refusing LAYER, because two layers can answer here and an arm that asserts only "refused" would stay green while its subject changed:
- missing: no gate at all -> `PRODUCT_CONTRACT_GATE_1_REQUIRED` at layer `GATE_1`.
- gate present, grant null -> `APPROVAL_HUMAN_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED` at layer `HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE`.
- agent-authored: grant whose principalKind is not "HUMAN" -> `APPROVAL_PRINCIPAL_NOT_HUMAN` at `HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE`.
- foreign-work: grant.workRef/gateId not matching the gate's, or either unnamed -> `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_BINDING_MISMATCH` at `HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE`.
- transplanted/stale: an internally valid grant whose workRef does not name THIS revision -> `PRODUCT_CONTRACT_GATE_1_BINDING_INVALID` at `GATE_1`.
POSITIVE ARM: build the only satisfying gate by CALLING the production `grantHumanAuthority` and feeding its returned gate in. Never hand-write a grant object, a signer, a principal kind or an approval record — this row's rail forbids synthesizing a positive fixture as production proof, and a hand-written grant would re-create the exact forgery the row closes.
Also assert that a refused Gate 1 still refuses `validateProductAcceptanceBinding` (the propagation at product-contract-acceptance-binding.ts:182), so a refusal confers no downstream acceptance.

Derive the positive: call `checkHumanAuthority(gate)` FIRST and, on refusal, RETURN IT VERBATIM — do not re-wrap it into a GATE_1 code, or the two-layer discrimination step 2's arms pin is destroyed and every grant-internal defect collapses into one indistinguishable code. Then require the gate's workRef to name THIS revision (contractId / revisionId / revisionDigest binding, matching the existing checks at :113-118); on mismatch refuse `PRODUCT_CONTRACT_GATE_1_BINDING_INVALID` at `GATE_1`.
TWO THINGS THAT WOULD REOPEN THE HOLE, both worth a comment in the code:
1. Import `checkHumanAuthority` INTRA-PACKAGE from `../planning/approval-authority.js`, exactly as `packages/core/src/planning/approval-policy.ts:27` already does. Do NOT publish it on the barrel: `packages/core/src/index.ts:224-231` documents that it stays unpublished on purpose, because a consumer able to call it could then decide for itself whether to honour the answer.
2. Do NOT route Gate 1 through the published `decideApprovalAuthority`. It falls through to `decidePolicy` when the gate is absent (approval-policy.ts:130-137), so a `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN` policy would satisfy Gate 1 — precisely the authority hole this row exists to close. Gate 1 refuses on an absent gate, unconditionally, and is never satisfiable by a policy value.
Keep `advisoryOnly: true` on the positive: this row makes the positive authority-derived, it does not promote Gate 1 from advisory to binding. The file is 198 lines against a 250 target; the deletions roughly offset the additions, so do not split it.

Two clauses, one fixture each in the suite.

STEP 6 (2 of 2) — ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FINDINGS.

(1) COULD A DIFFERENT LAYER ANSWER FIRST? Walked every arm against the actual order in gateResult (absent -> readGate structural -> checkHumanAuthority -> Gate 1 revision binding):
- unsatisfied gate: fixture is productContractGate1Authority(revision) itself, so gateId and workRef are CORRECT for this revision. Gate 1's own fence would have PASSED; only the kernel can answer. Not maskable.
- agent-authored / moment-invalid / grant-side workRef or gateId moved: the GATE-side fields stay correct in every one of these fixtures, so Gate 1's fence would have passed and the kernel is the only refuser. Not maskable.
- gate.workRef = "": here BOTH layers would refuse. The kernel answers first, which is what the arm asserts. Falsifiability preserved: deleting the kernel's namedRef clause makes this fall through to GATE_1 and the arm still reds, on a different code.
- transplanted (stale digest, and gate-2 id): the grant is internally consistent, so the kernel PASSES and only Gate 1 can refuse. Not maskable. The stale fixture additionally asserts staleRevision.revisionDigest !== revision.revisionDigest, so it cannot go vacuous if the two drafts ever converge.
Drill B empirically confirms the split: it reds the four kernel-layer arms and leaves all three GATE_1-layer arms green.

(2) ANY ARM ASSERTING ONLY "refused"? No. The `refusal()` helper asserts ok === false and then RETURNS [code, layer]; every one of its call sites compares that pair with toEqual. The two root-surface assertions use `x.ok ? "SATISFIED" : [x.code, x.layer]` so a wrongly-satisfied result reds with a legible value rather than a truthiness miss. Case count asserted nonzero on the generated table: expect(cases.length).toBe(6).

(3) DID A HAND-WRITTEN GRANT CREEP BACK IN AS A POSITIVE? No. The only producer of a satisfied gate anywhere in the suite is `grantedGate`, which calls production grantHumanAuthority over productContractGate1Authority. `withGrant` only DEGRADES a minted grant to build negatives. The old approval literal survives solely as a negative fixture, in both the focused suite and index-surface.test.ts.

(4) DOES A GATE 1 REFUSAL STILL BLOCK ACCEPTANCE? Yes: validateProductAcceptanceBinding returns the gate refusal before reading graph or acceptance, and the 6-class table asserts both the code+layer AND that the result carries no acceptanceCriteriaDigest.

FURTHER FINDINGS FROM THE HOSTILE-INPUT / STATE PASS, none blocking:
- TOCTOU: readGate snapshots ONCE and hands the SNAPSHOT (never the caller's object) to checkHumanAuthority, so a caller mutating its object after the call cannot change an answer already derived. snapshotData refuses accessors, proxies, symbol keys, cycles and exotic prototypes, so no getter runs. Arrays are rejected by exact()/isRecord.
- `grant: undefined` (as opposed to null) is refused structurally as GATE_1_BINDING_INVALID rather than as APPROVAL_HUMAN_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED. That is off-contract input for `HumanAuthorityGrant | null`, it fails closed, and it is the one place readGate answers before the kernel. Recorded rather than "fixed", because adding a null-normalising branch would be an unfalsifiable duplicate of the kernel's own check.
- APPROVAL_PRINCIPAL_MISSING is unreachable through Gate 1 — but it is unreachable through checkHumanAuthority generally, since that function builds the principal object itself. No arm was written for a code no input can produce.
- DELIBERATE LOOSENING, disclosed: Gate 1 no longer bounds principal-id length. The old readApproval applied boundedRef (<= 512 bytes) to the approval's principalId; the new path takes principalId from the minted GRANT, and the authority kernel requires only a non-empty trimmed string. The removed arm `principalId: "x".repeat(513) -> BINDING_INVALID` therefore no longer describes Gate 1's job. Re-imposing the bound here would duplicate an identity-admission concern at a second layer and create exactly the dead-guard pattern this board has been bitten by. The value is only ever compared for equality against a derived string; it is not stored, echoed or parsed.
- Purity/concurrency: every function in the changed path is pure, allocates its own WeakSet per call, mutates no shared state, performs no IO, and freezes what it returns. Running twice concurrently is indistinguishable from running twice in sequence.
